title.narrative: Curriculum and Lecturer Development Programme for the Maritime and Energy Sector

description.narrative:
The proposed project must contribute to the following ++objective++:
- Contribute to inclusive sustainable development and end poverty in all its forms (SDG 1)
The proposed project must contribute to the following ++long-term impact++:
- Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy; and - Maritime sector operates in accordance with international (security and skills) requirements, creating more jobs and added value in infrastructural (transport) development.
The following ++medium-term impact++ will contribute to this:
(I) Education system (TVET/HE) is of good quality, relevant and accessible (SDG 4);
(II) Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG 17);
(III) Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce.
This will be achieved by the following ++outcome++:
B. Enhanced knowledge and skills of individuals and organisations (in partner countries and in the NL) in line with country/regional specific labour market needs and aiming at inclusiveness.
To that end, the following ++output(s)++ must be achieved by the end of the project:
1. Develop and implement training for the instructors and lecturers 2. Develop curriculum and execution of training courses 3. Project result dissemination and sustainability

description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Outputs TMT+ out of proposal:
1. Provision of relevant training and curricula. Everything ESCN is using for learning is outdated and no longer relevant. Consideration needs to be given to the provision of the required training aids to support both education as well as short courses. 2. Upskilling of the teachers. There was explicit consent during the meeting that the teachers are not current and lack the experience and the required skills to teach the updated curriculum. In addition, they lack the skills to review and revise course content to keep it aligned with the STCW Code.
With the following Work Plan:
The project execution is divided into 3outputs, including several sub-outputs:
- Output 1: Didactical Training& Teaching -Output 1.1: IMO 6.09(Training Course for Instructors/teachers) -Output 1.2: IMO 6.10 (Training Course for Instructor on the use of a simulator as an educational tool) -Output 1.3: IMO 3.12 (Assessor and Assessment)
- Output 2: Curricula Development& Course Execution-Output 2.1: Curricula Development for several courses-Output 2.2: Execution of the courses as developed
- Output 3: Project Dissemination & Sustainability-Output 3.1: Kick-off session-Output 3.2: Gender policy study & workshop-Output 3.3: Closing ceremony/seminars
The following overview indicates what has been provided throughout the project in 2020: OHS Maritime Training (8-13 December 2019), Maritime Law & Regulations (10-14 February 2020), IMO Course Model 6.09 (17-21 February 2020), IMO Course Model 6.10 - 3.12 (9-17 March 2020 - not completed due to COVID) . As can be seen, the train-the-trainer courses could not be completed on location due to Covid travel restrictions. Hence the request for an extension to develop and complete these courses online.
To conclude: the intended courses could not be completed in time.

Outputs TMT+ out of proposal:
Provision of relevant training and curricula. Everything ESCN is using for learning is outdated and no longer relevant. Consideration needs to be given to the provision of the required training aids to support both education as well as short courses.
Upskilling of the teachers. There was explicit consent during the meeting that the teachers are not current and lack the experience and the required skills to teach the updated curriculum. In addition, they lack the skills to review and revise course content to keep it aligned with the STCW Code.
With the following Work Plan:
The project execution is divided into 3outputs, including several sub-outputs:
Output 1: Didactical Training& Teaching -Output 1.1: IMO 6.09(Training Course for Instructors/teachers)-Output 1.2: IMO 6.10 (Training Course for Instructor on the use of a simulator as an educational tool)-Output 1.3: IMO 3.12(Assessor and Assessment)
Output 2: Curricula Development& Course Execution-Output 2.1: Curricula Development for several courses-Output 2.2: Execution of the courses as developed
Output 3: Project Dissemination & Sustainability-Output 3.1: Kick-off session-Output 3.2: Gender policy study & workshop-Output 3.3: Closing ceremony/seminars
The following overview indicates what has been provided throughout the project in 2021 (and 2022); see attached file. As can be seen, all courses were developed and knowledge was transmitted as per the project plan output 1 and 2. Output 3 has been completed, except for output 3.3: Closing ceremony/seminars. The two reasons for not providing output 3.3 have been a time constraint as well as budget constraint.
The budget constraint resulted from the many hours that had to be put into the development of online courses, as well as much higher travel costs after the Covid restrictions were lifted.

comment.narrative:
5 active people in the maritime and energy labour market in Mozambique
2 businesses active in Mozambique in the maritime and energy sector
​

17-09-2023: To the Project Manager knowledge none of the graduates is self-employed, which is also the answer received from ESCN. This could have changed over the time of reporting. Starting as a self-employed person in Mozambique is a bigger challenge than we know of in Western-Europe.
Correction on the previous question as to the knowledge institution that performs better: 1 Institute (ESCN) performs better. ESCN is also the institute that is able to perform better in the short run as the developed and provided knowledge and understanding can be transferred one to one curriculum and teaching methods (e.g. the IMO courses). During the lecturers teaching time at ESCN it has been shown clear that ESCN staff/teaching has improved tremendously and we have seen the direct better performance.
All other institutes: this must prove itself in the long-run and would need further evaluation and follow-up.
